protections: A seed wheel fetched by `pip download` must be authenticated against the authoritative PyPI release record for the distribution/version it claims before it is returned to a seeder; today download_wheel decides nothing and returns whatever pip left in the folder (src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/acquire.py:140-142).

A wheel replayed from the persisted app-data update log must be the wheel that was authenticated, not merely the file currently at <app_data>/wheel/house/<stored filename> (src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/periodic_update.py:53-56, :68-72).

The install image that seeding uses must be derived from authenticated wheel bytes; today the image is keyed only on installer class + wheel stem and is never rebuilt once present (src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/via_app_data.py:67-70, src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py:219-220).

Wheels shipped inside the package are authenticated on load against the compiled-in sha256 table (src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/embed/__init__.py:96-108) - the one place in this tree where this protection already exists, and it covers only BUNDLE_FOLDER.

masking: A wheel rejected by a new download check is still left in app_data.house (acquire.py:129-132), so the replay route (T4) and the image route (T6) only become observable as separate bugs once the download check exists and refuses a file; before that the poison is simply used everywhere and nothing looks wrong.

The wheel image (T6) hides the wheel from every later check: once wheel/<py>/image/1/<installer>/<stem> exists, the wheel file is never opened again (via_app_data.py:156-160, pip_install/base.py:219-220), so a fix placed only on acquisition never runs on the seeding path that actually copies files into the venv.

T2's house fallback is masked by T1's success: as long as download_wheel returns whatever pip wrote, nobody notices that the fallback branch (acquire.py:157-172) can return a file pip never downloaded; it becomes a distinct hole the moment T1's check is added only on the 'Saved ' branch.

T8 can only shadow the verified bundle when IS_ZIPAPP is true (app_data/base.py:93-97); in a normal source checkout the bundled path is yielded directly, so the route is invisible until the zipapp layout is considered.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1 (reject any wheel whose sha256 does not equal PyPI's) rejects the private-mirror, offline and private-distribution cases that acquire.py:134 and acquire.py:175-192 make supported configurations; the guard has to have a third 'not verifiable -> allow' outcome, so the same site carries both the hidden requirement and the must-keep-working value.

Checking a replayed wheel against PyPI needs a digest the producer never stored (periodic_update.py:94-104, :134-140), while the existing contract allows a log entry whose file is absent from the house (tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_bundle.py:63-66); recording a digest at download time and re-verifying when the file exists are two separate changes that must agree.

Keying the image on wheel bytes (or invalidating it after a rejected download) forces rebuilds of wheel/<py>/image/1/... on every content change, while tests/unit/seed/embed/test_bootstrap_link_via_app_data.py:105-110 asserts a second create reuses the cache and produces identical site-packages; the fix has to invalidate on mismatch without breaking ordinary reuse.

Verifying --extra-search-dir wheels against PyPI is only safe under the same 'not on PyPI -> allow' rule; otherwise a private wheel placed there (bundle.py:54-59) fails to seed, which is the documented purpose of the option (base_embed.py:109-116).

fairness_risks: Custom/private index: acquire.py:134 forwards the caller's environment into the pip subprocess, so PIP_INDEX_URL / PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL / PIP_INDEX legitimately change where the wheel comes from; a rule that requires PyPI's digest rejects a wheel served by exactly the configured source.

Offline or proxied installs: the only metadata source used in this tree fails closed to None (periodic_update.py:388-405); treating 'no metadata' as a mismatch breaks air-gapped environment creation, so 'unverifiable' must mean allow.

Private/local distributions and wheels whose filename is not a PyPI release file must be let through (the published fix's own branches, per the screener's O6 shapes); refusing them breaks private packaging.
--extra-search-dir is a documented user trust boundary (base_embed.py:109-116); enforcing PyPI digests there contradicts the contract unless the unverifiable case is allowed.

PipInvoke's --download path deliberately leaves the index enabled; tests/unit/seed/embed/test_pip_invoke.py:45 asserts '--no-index' is absent, so a fix that adds it to close T7 breaks a documented flag and its regression test.

The update log is deliberately metadata-only: tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_bundle.py:63-66 expects a Wheel for a log entry whose file need not exist in the house, so a replay check must tolerate a missing file rather than turning the cache into an error.
Wheel-image reuse is a tested behaviour (tests/unit/seed/embed/test_bootstrap_link_via_app_data.py:105-110); any content-keyed cache must still produce the same site-packages on the second create.

A pip.conf / PIP_CONFIG_FILE index redirect is invisible to an env-based gate (the published fix's documented limitation per the screener); a gate reading only the three env vars leaves a supported configuration unverified, and a gate that also reads config files changes behaviour for users who never set the env vars.

Refused input shape that legitimate use needs: a wheel whose filename differs from PyPI's canonical filename for the same release (build tag, local version suffix) must not be treated as a mismatch when its bytes are the published artefact.

design.why: Four independent judgements in four different files/packages, each with a different reason a solver can honestly stand down: T1 'pip already fetched it over HTTPS and exited 0'; T4 'it was hashed when it was downloaded, the log is only metadata'; T5 'the user named that directory'; T6 'the image was built from a wheel that had already passed the check'. T1's group is where the DeepSeek-shaped trap and the MiMo-shaped trap sit together: the protection is simply absent (T1) while the same site carries the coupled must-keep-working value that private mirrors/offline/private names are legitimate (T9), so a pass/fail check either misses the hole or over-hardens and breaks supported configurations; T4 is the producer-off-the-check's-path trap (the log turns a stored filename into a Wheel without reading it) and rewards the solver who extends the log schema or re-verifies on replay; T5 is a second absent-protection route with a strong dismissal; T6 is a proxy-object trap (the image cache decides on the stem, not the bytes) that no acquisition-time check reaches. Every one is testable offline with mocked Popen/urlopen and a local wheel file, and each needs a different mechanism to fix (verify returned bytes with a three-way outcome plus cleanup, extend the producer/replay, verify only when the name is a PyPI release, key or invalidate the image). Fixing only the sink the report names leaves three of the four open, which is exactly the stacking this checkout supports. Alternatives left out: T7 (PipInvoke index resolution) is a real second implementation but its 'correct' behaviour contradicts the --download flag asserted at test_pip_invoke.py:45; T8 is zipapp-only (app_data/base.py:93-97) so it is not reachable in an unpacked checkout; T11 (cached None fails open) is a property of whichever lookup the fix chooses rather than a site of its own; T2/T3/T9/T10 belong to T1's group because one correctly written guard at download_wheel closes or must honour them.
